web_evidence.title: Book Review: A Week in Winter by Maeve Binchy
web_evidence.note: The reviewer explicitly describes an all-knowing third-person narrator and explains that the ten chapters rotate among temporary protagonists, establishing changing focal characters rather than changing grammatical person.

person_note: The book’s base voice is an omniscient third-person narrator that shifts focal attention among Chicky, Anders, Winnie, and the other chapter protagonists. These viewpoint shifts remain third person and therefore do not constitute ALTERNATING narration. The many quoted instances of “I” and “you” are character speech, while q00477 contains diagnostic third-person base narration despite its upstream dialogue bucket. The authorized opening, an interior publisher-sourced attribution, the input passage, and an explicit whole-book structural description agree. The main coverage limitation is that the Tier A excerpt is confined to the opening, but the independent interior and whole-book evidence resolves that limitation without credible contrary evidence.
